standard_prerequisites.name: Emptiness of the fibre of a closed set at a point spreads to an open subset of the closure, and fibres over a point are Jacobson schemes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, label more-morphisms-lemma-empty-generic-fibre (proof line 4562); Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-ubiquity-Jacobson-schemes (proof line 4566)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that, having assumed the morphism locally of finitely presented, the vanishing of the fibre of the closure at t persists on an open subset of the closure of t, and since the fibre over s is Jacobson it contains a closed point where the fibre still vanishes.

core_obligations: Replace the morphism by a locally finitely presented one: apply the separation lemma to the point t and the closure Z of the impurity point xi, obtaining an open neighbourhood V of t, a morphism b : T' -> S locally of finite presentation, and a closed subscheme Z' disjoint from the fibre of Z' over a(t) and containing the image of Z over V; replace T by V, note that the image xi' of xi is still a relative associated point by base change of the relative assassin, and that its closure lies in Z' and so avoids the fibre over a(t), which makes the lifted triple an impurity (proof lines 4522-4557).

Make the specialisation point closed in the fibre: now that the morphism is locally of finite presentation, the closure Z of xi has empty fibre over t by assumption, so by the spreading-out lemma the fibre of Z is empty at every point of an open subset of the closure of t; since the fibre of the morphism over s is a Jacobson scheme, that open subset contains a closed point t'' of the closure of t, and the triple with the specialisation from t' to t'' is again an impurity (proof lines 4559-4569).
proof_roadmap: Use the separation lemma to replace the base by a locally finitely presented model and lift the impurity to it (proof lines 4522-4557).
Spread the vanishing of the fibre along the closure of the specialisation point and pick a closed point of the fibre where it still vanishes (proof lines 4559-4569).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that any impurity of a module above a point can be replaced by an impurity whose morphism is locally of finite presentation and whose specialisation point is closed in the fibre over the given point (statement lines 4513-4520, tag 05FX). The proof does two concrete things: it uses the separation lemma to build a locally finitely presented replacement morphism together with a closed subscheme that keeps the closure of the impurity point away from the special fibre, and then, using that the fibre is a Jacobson scheme, it produces a closed point of the closure of the original point at which the fibre of the closure is still empty so that the specialisation may be shortened. The Jacobson closed point step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
